proposal.hypothesis: Replacing pointwise long_view BCE with correctly signed same-user BPR will improve within-user ordering and the candidate's marginal contribution to the current portfolio without sacrificing the engagement-head regularization.
proposal.implementation_plan: Replace only the main long_view optimization path of w002 with vectorized same-user BPR while retaining its categorical DeepFM representation and four pointwise engagement auxiliary heads. In the model block, define a DeepFM with globally offset categorical embeddings, first-order terms, the existing [128,64] deep branch, one ranking logit, and engagement auxiliary logits. In the train block, use splits['train'].user_id[train_idx] and y['main'] to build contiguous per-user positive and negative pools for users containing both classes. Each epoch samples one same-user negative per positive with the seeded NumPy generator. In the loss block, compute mean softplus(-(z_pos-z_neg)); verify at zero difference that the positive gradient is -0.5/pair_count and combine this main loss with the incumbent auxiliary BCE at weight 0.2. Keep k=16, lr=0.001, l2=0.0001, batch=8192, 12 epochs, and the fixed train-only checkpoint policy unchanged.
proposal.justification: Same-user BPR directly trains the score differences used by both metrics and avoids spending main-loss capacity on user-level prevalence or other per-user constants. Retaining the incumbent auxiliary heads isolates the tested change to the main ranking objective.

research_evidence.query: Which ranking objective and sampling implementation reliably improves the official FM?
research_evidence.reason: Cold-start runs repeatedly proposed BPR but implementation quality varied sharply.
research_evidence.summary: Use vectorized same-user BPR, not all-batch quadratic pairing. Build per-user positive blocks and negative pools only for users with both classes; use one sampled same-user negative per positive per epoch; align positive and negative arrays by user block; return safely when no eligible pairs; the FM global bias cancels. The exact loss is L=mean(softplus(-(z_pos-z_neg))). With diff=z_pos-z_neg, use g_pos=(sigmoid(diff)-1)/pair_count and g_neg=-g_pos. At diff=0, g_pos must equal -0.5/pair_count, never +0.5/pair_count; a one-step sanity check must increase z_pos-z_neg. At k=16, lr=0.001, one negative, the five-seed official-validation primary changed from 0.601500738 ± 0.000481897 for pointwise FM to 0.603517127 ± 0.000631158 for BPR. Treat the mechanism and implementation invariants as the prior; rerun it inside the Agent harness rather than assuming the measured delta transfers exactly.

experiment_contract.claim: The experiment tests whether censored train-only watch-time supervision improves and diversifies the existing DeepFM ranking representation.
experiment_contract.expected_observable: Training metadata must report positive incomplete and completed auxiliary counts, zero included rows with invalid watch ratio or zero duration, and a finite nonzero watch-head loss.
experiment_contract.falsification_condition: The hypothesis is refuted if trusted marginal portfolio primary is non-positive, or invalid-target auditing shows leakage or incorrect censoring; absence of consumed watch rows invalidates rather than confirms the experiment.

Mask invalid ratios and all zero-duration rows from the watch loss.

proposal.hypothesis: A leakage-safe censored watch-time auxiliary will teach duration-sensitive item-quality interactions not fully captured by the four sparse engagement heads, yielding complementary within-user ordering and positive marginal contribution to the heterogeneous portfolio.
proposal.implementation_plan: Add one censored watch-time regression head to a visible reproduction of the w002 DeepFM while leaving native long_view as the main pointwise label and retaining its four engagement heads. In the target block, call DV.watch_ratio() on train only, combine valid ratios with splits['train'].duration_ms to derive played_ms, and construct scaled log targets log1p(played_ms)/12 and log-duration bounds log1p(duration_ms)/12. Mark completed observations where valid and played_ms>=duration_ms; exclude invalid ratios and zero-duration rows from this auxiliary loss. In the model block, attach a scalar watch head to the same shared FM/deep representation used by the ranking and engagement heads. In the train block, use exact regression residual loss for incomplete plays and a one-sided lower-bound hinge for completed plays that becomes zero once the prediction reaches the log-duration bound. Add this auxiliary at fixed weight 0.2, with all other architecture and optimization settings held to the parent values.
proposal.justification: Watch time supplies a denser training signal than rare engagement actions, while censoring avoids penalizing completed plays whose latent desired watch time may exceed the video duration. Shared embeddings can transfer this signal to the long_view ranker without exposing post-exposure feedback at inference.
proposal.observation: The current parent has four engagement auxiliary heads but no watch-time head; train has 24076 zero-duration rows, so explicit validity masking is necessary rather than treating every watch ratio as an exact regression target.

research_evidence.query: How should watch time complement native long_view without changing evaluation labels?
research_evidence.reason: The native binary label discards engagement magnitude and completed plays are right-censored by duration.
research_evidence.summary: Keep native long_view as the ranking objective and add a small censored watch-time regression head sharing FM embeddings. Transform play time and duration with log1p/12. For incomplete plays use exact regression residual; for completed plays use a one-sided lower-bound hinge that stops penalizing predictions above log-duration. Never use evaluation-period feedback as an input feature. BPR plus this auxiliary target at weight 0.2 reached five-seed official-validation primary 0.604023290 ± 0.000282947 versus 0.603517127 ± 0.000631158 for BPR alone; on three random-exposure seeds, unbiased primary was 0.376328528 ± 0.003245064 versus 0.373291085 ± 0.002151737. This is an implementation prior, not permission to replace the fixed relevance label.

Watch behavior can encode exposure-policy bias and reduce robustness despite being dense.
The fixed auxiliary weight may overemphasize duration relative to top-five relevance.
Incorrect completion or validity masking would turn censoring into label noise.

selection_rationale: Candidate 0 is the only viable candidate. It is a structural, error-diversifying refinement of w002 rather than scalar-only tuning: a censored watch-time head is connected explicitly through train-only target construction, the shared DeepFM representation, and a consumed auxiliary loss. Its exact-dataset mechanism evidence is adapted conservatively because the prior used BPR while this experiment retains the parent's pointwise long_view objective; thus the prior score is not treated as directly comparable. Implementation reliability is supported by explicit masking of the 24076 zero-duration rows, separate incomplete and completed censoring losses, auditable consumption counts, and a clear prohibition on post-exposure inference features. Although reproducing the registry-owned parent and exposure-policy bias create risk, the candidate has a credible path to marginal portfolio gain through duration-sensitive rank changes and complementary errors, with a falsifiable non-positive marginal-gain rejection rule. With no competing viable candidate or stated exact matching negative result, it is selected.
